question.text: How many new suspected measles cases will Bangladesh's DGHS report for the 24 hours to 8:00 am on 13 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves using the DGHS (Directorate General of Health Services, Bangladesh) daily measles bulletin — published in Bengali as "হাম প্রেস রিলিজ" — covering the 24 hours from 8:00 am Bangladesh Standard Time (UTC+6) on 12 November 2026 to 8:00 am on 13 November 2026, which is listed at https://dghs.gov.bd/pages/press-releases (mirrored at https://dghs.gov.bd/pages/news). The resolved value is the bulletin's 24-hour figure for newly identified suspected measles cases (patients with measles-like symptoms) — i.e. the suspected-case line, not the combined suspected-plus-confirmed figure, not laboratory-confirmed cases alone, and not hospital admissions; a value of 1,300 new suspected cases resolves as 1,300. If the bulletin's 24-hour suspected figure cannot be obtained, the value is instead computed as the cumulative suspected-case total reported in the bulletin dated 13 November 2026 minus that reported in the bulletin dated 12 November 2026. If the DGHS bulletin itself cannot be accessed or read at all, the value as reported for that same bulletin by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: The bulletin is normally released in the afternoon (local time) of the date it covers; if the 13 November 2026 bulletin is delayed, resolution waits for it rather than annulling. The resolved value is the figure as first published for that bulletin, and any later upward or downward revision by DGHS of that day's count does not change the resolution. If no DGHS bulletin covering a period ending 8:00 am on 13 November 2026 (and no reporting of one) exists at all, the question is annulled.

research:
## 1. Resolution source

- 2026-11-02: The DGHS press-release page (https://dghs.gov.bd/pages/press-releases) lists daily "হাম প্রেস রিলিজ" entries through 01/11/2026, plus one entry each day back to 23/10. There are 213 entries in total, and the site was last updated 2 Nov at 18:48. The bulletin attachments are not plain links in the page HTML, so I could not read the PDFs or images themselves. [DGHS](https://dghs.gov.bd/pages/press-releases)
- Latest value I found, from the bulletin for the 24 hours to 8:00 am on Mon 2 Nov: **1,492 new suspected cases**, 56 confirmed, cumulative suspected 231,505, cumulative confirmed 23,991, 3 suspected deaths (1,152 suspected plus 105 confirmed deaths), and 1,385 suspected-case admissions. Dhaka division had 574 and Chattogram 311. This comes from media coverage, not the bulletin itself. [tob.news](https://tob.news/3-die-with-suspected-measles-1492-new-cases-in-24hrs/)

## 2. Current status

- Nothing has settled the question yet. The resolving bulletin (13 Nov, a Friday, covering Thursday 8 am to Friday 8 am) has not been published.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-11-02: 1,492 suspected cases, the highest daily figure in this recent run. The cumulative totals agree: 231,505 − 230,013 = 1,492. [tob.news](https://tob.news/3-die-with-suspected-measles-1492-new-cases-in-24hrs/); [Daily Waadaa](https://www.dailywaadaa.com/health/2026/11/02/three-more-children-die-with-measles-symptoms)
- 2026-11-01: 1,353 suspected cases, cumulative 230,013. Reports disagree on new confirmed cases (64 or 68). This came from search summaries, and I could not confirm it against a primary source. [Observer BD](https://observerbd.com/news/603195) (403 when fetched)
- 2026-10-31 (Saturday bulletin): I could not find any media figure. Working back from the cumulative totals, it was about **987** (230,013 − 1,353 − 227,673). That is unverified and assumes the 1 Nov figure is suspected-only.
- 2026-10-30: 1,316 suspected cases, cumulative 227,673 (the 29 Oct cumulative was 226,357, which matches). [Financial Express via search](https://thefinancialexpress.com.bd/national/two-more-children-die-with-measles-like-symptoms); [TBS](https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/measles-toll-reaches-1249-7-more-children-die-1586781)
- 2026-11-01/02: Dengue is surging at the same time (1,970 hospitalised in 24 h on 2 Nov; 173 deaths in October), which may strain the same reporting system. [Daily Star](https://www.thedailystar.net/news/healthcare/disease/news/6-die-dengue-1970-hospitalised-24-hours-4313826)

## 4. Base rates

- Recent daily suspected counts: 1,306 (15 Oct) [Daily Star](https://www.thedailystar.net/news/healthcare/disease/news/4-more-die-measles-symptoms-24-hours-4299581); 1,232 (27 Oct); 1,322 (28 Oct); 1,251 (29 Oct); 1,316 (30 Oct); about 987 (31 Oct, derived); 1,353 (1 Nov); 1,492 (2 Nov).
- Implied averages: 15 to 18 Oct averaged about 1,123 a day (213,244 − 209,876 over 3 bulletins). 18 to 30 Oct averaged about 1,202 a day (227,673 − 213,244 over 12). 30 Oct to 2 Nov averaged about 1,277 a day.
- WHO SEARO counted 8,216 suspected cases in week 42 (12-18 Oct), about 1,174 a day, and said there has been "no steady decline" since early September.
- **Possible weekday pattern:** the Saturday bulletins (31 Oct about 987, and probably 17 Oct) look low. That fits fewer reports on Friday, the weekend day. The 13 Nov bulletin is a Friday release covering mostly Thursday. The most recent Friday bulletin (30 Oct) was 1,316. I checked this pattern on only a few weeks, so it is weak evidence.
- Earlier comparison points: 980 (26 Sep), 1,255 (29 Sep), 1,148 (around 20 Sep). The trend from late September to early November is flat to slightly rising, with daily swings of roughly ±10-15% and occasional Saturday dips of about 20-25%.
- Reporting caveat: news outlets sometimes give the suspected-plus-confirmed figure. For example, on 29 Oct the combined figure was 1,315 against 1,251 suspected-only.

## 5. Other forecasts

- I found no prediction market or expert forecast for daily measles counts in Bangladesh. The Kalshi measles markets you listed are about US case counts and US elimination status, and the Polymarket Bangladesh markets are cricket. None of them match this question.
- WHO SEARO (21 Oct) gives the only expert framing I found: a plateau at about 1,000-1,300 a day.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (13 Nov)

- Daily DGHS bulletins from 3 to 12 Nov will show whether the 1,492 on 2 Nov is a one-day spike or the start of a rise.
- The measles-rubella catch-up campaign (started 26 Sep, about 3.4M children) could start to lower incidence, or push up detection and reporting.
- Any revisions or reporting delays could matter: the question resolves on the first-published figure, and the cumulative difference is the fallback.
- A government or ministry response to the EPI review report (submitted late October) could come in this period.
- The next WHO SEARO epidemiological bulletin may give week 43-44 totals.

Not found: the 31 Oct bulletin figure, direct reads of the bulletin PDFs, and any market on this metric.

What the series shows (all averages are my calculations from cumulative totals):
- **Weekday effect:** Saturday bulletins, which cover Friday (the weekend), run low: 1,014 and 987. Friday bulletins, which cover Thursday, were 1,110 and 1,316.
- **Rising trend:**
  - 14 Oct to 30 Oct: about 1,194 a day.
  - 18 to 23 Oct: about 1,125 a day.
  - 24 to 30 Oct: about 1,258 a day.
  - 31 Oct to 2 Nov: about 1,277 a day.
  - Since mid-October the counts have drifted up, not down.
- **Earlier context:** about 1,171 a day from 10 Sep to 14 Oct. WHO SEARO counted about 1,000 to 1,300 a day since early September with no steady decline, and 8,216 suspected cases in week 42 (about 1,174 a day). [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Bangladesh_measles_outbreak)
- **Spread:** On non-Saturday days in the last two weeks the range was about 1,110 to 1,492. That is roughly ±10 to 15% around about 1,300.
- **Watch for combined figures:** Some outlets report suspected plus confirmed cases together. Confirmed cases have recently added about 55 to 90 a day.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on Bangladesh's daily measles counts. The Kalshi measles markets are about US case counts and are not relevant.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Daily DGHS bulletins from 3 to 12 Nov will show the trend. The 7 Nov bulletin (Saturday) will likely be a low, weekend-affected day.
- WHO SEARO's next epidemiological bulletin may give weekly totals for weeks 43 and 44.
- Possible effects from the measles-rubella vaccination campaign that started 26 Sep, and from the independent review of the immunisation programme (EPI) recommendations.
- Possible strain on reporting from the dengue surge.
- I found no scheduled holiday on 12 or 13 Nov that would change reporting. Verify this.

(f) **Experts and markets:** WHO SEARO describes a plateau of about 1,000-1,300 a day with "no steady decline." There are no relevant markets.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- Low: Reporting disruption from dengue overload, a holiday or data-entry lag, or a real decline as campaign effects kick in, could produce a count near 800-950.
- High: Renewed acceleration, for example spread in the Dhaka and Chattogram divisions, could produce 1,700-1,900. So could a catch-up batch of delayed reports being added to one day.

(f) **Experts and markets:** There is no market or expert forecast on this quantity. WHO describes the counts as roughly 1,000 to 1,300 per day with "no steady decline".

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- Low: Reporting is incomplete because of dengue strain on staff or a data-system glitch, or the campaign produces a sharp decline. The count could then fall to about 700 to 900.
- High: A reporting backlog is cleared, there is a real surge in Dhaka or Chattogram, or the figure is confused with the combined suspected-plus-confirmed count. The count could then reach about 1,700 to 1,950.
